characterization_methods.key_findings: κ'-carbide is coherent with the austenite matrix with a cube-on-cube orientation relationship; L'12 ordering diffraction patterns observed; planar slip and shearable κ' precipitates identified.
characterization_methods.purpose: To characterize intragranular κ'-carbide precipitation, ordering and γ/κ' interfaces

characterization_methods.key_findings: The κ-carbide shows depletion of both interstitial C and substitutional Al relative to the ideal stoichiometric bulk perovskite; off-stoichiometric Al explained by strain from the κ/γ mismatch facilitating occupation of Al sites by Mn atoms.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Fe-30Mn-7.7Al-1.3C alloy aged at 600 °C for 24 h
characterization_methods.purpose: To measure the chemical composition of κ-carbide

characterization_methods.key_findings: Plastic deformation occurs by formation and propagation of straight slip bands regardless of heat treatment; separation distance between slip bands increases with aging time (29, 36, 45 nm).
characterization_methods.purpose: To observe plastic deformation (slip band formation) and precipitate morphology
characterization_methods.technique: Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) / Electron channelling contrast imaging (ECCI)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Bright second-phase particles nucleate on austenite grain boundaries, develop into a lamellar (γ+κ+α) colony, and coarsen into large interpenetrating colonies with increasing time.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C austenitic steel isothermally held at 700 °C for 1, 25 and 100 h
characterization_methods.purpose: To observe the growing feature of κ' in austenite and evolution of κ* in (κ+γ+α) lamellar colonies on austenite grain boundaries

characterization_methods.key_findings: The κ-precipitates were not observed by X-ray diffraction measurement in this steel (region-similar to SIP steel).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Fe-27Mn-11.5Al-0.95C after solution treatment at 1050 °C and water quenching

characterization_methods.key_findings: Peak hardness increases for longer times at lower aging temperatures; higher C content raises peak strength and accelerates aging kinetics.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Aging at 450–600 °C for times up to 1000 h (in air)
characterization_methods.purpose: To establish age-hardening curves of austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys

analytical_models.equation_role: predicts equilibrium phase constitution of austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels including stability of κ-carbide
analytical_models.model_note: Used to calculate equilibrium phase proportions vs temperature.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Iron-rich Fe-Mn-Al-C quaternary system; isothermal sections at 900 °C for Mn = 10/20/30%; polythermal sections for Fe-15Mn-xAl-yC, Fe-Mn-Al-0.85C
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: FSstel database (suppressing graphite formation); Connétable Fe-Al-C database; Chin et al. quaternary Fe-Al-Mn-C description
computational_details.software_used: FactSage 6.4 (FSstel database); Thermo-Calc Steels database; CALPHAD-type description
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated phase boundaries deviate from experiments; FactSage underestimates formation temperatures of κ-carbide and M23C6 by 100 °C and 150 °C respectively in a Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C alloy; no M7C3 found experimentally though predicted.

analytical_models.equation_role: predicts SFE and USFE as a function of Mn/Al/C distribution and ordering
analytical_models.model_note: Al and C as well as Mn at concentrations higher than 15 at.% increase the SFE; Mn–C pair formation and Al-ordering restrain SFE growth.

computational_details.potential_model_or_database: First-principles (ab initio) modelling of Mn, Al and C distribution and SFE in austenite
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Explains observed planar glide before mechanical twinning regardless of SFE; short-range Al-ordering strongly decreases the unstable stacking fault energy (USFE) but does not affect the SFE.

analytical_models.equation_role: predicts the deformation mechanism (TRIP/TWIP/MBIP/κ) from composition
analytical_models.model_note: Mn decreases SFE in the range 0–15/20% and increases it by 1.2–3 mJ/m2 per wt% Mn at higher Mn; Si and Cr decrease SFE.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fe-Mn-Al-C austenite at room temperature; Al 2–12 wt%, Mn 10–50 wt%, C 0–1.5 wt%
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Composition-dependent SFE maps (3D surfaces) coupled to deformation-mechanism fields
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: SFE maps partition the composition space into TRIP, TWIP, MBIP, MBIP+Kappa and TWIP+Kappa fields delimited by iso-SFE 20 and 50 mJ/m2 contours and the kappa-carbide forming border.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Planar slip bands form by shearing of κ'-carbide precipitates by dislocations; the separation distance between slip bands increases with aging time (29, 36, 45 nm for as-solutionized, 3 h aged, 10 h aged Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.8C). Taylor lattice dislocation structures have been observed at γ/κ'-carbide interfaces. When the size and volume fraction of κ' precipitates are large, a high chance exists for dislocations to meet and shear them.

interfaces.interface_notes: In the γ (FCC) matrix the lattice parameter of the κ phase is 0.383–0.386 nm and γ/κ interfaces are coherent (lattice mismatch < 3%). κ* develops originally as discrete particles but soon becomes thin films distributed continuously along γ grain boundaries.
interfaces.phase_evolution: γ → γ' + γ'' → γ' + L12(SRO) → γ' + κ' (spinodal decomposition → SRO → κ'). With prolonged aging κ' accumulates C and Al, the κ lattice parameter increases, the parent phase lattice parameter decreases, coherency is lost and a plate-like morphology develops. At high aging temperatures grain-boundary κ* forms (b0124, b0129, b0134).
interfaces.slip_behavior: Dislocation planar glide is dominant in aged austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels regardless of SFE and aging conditions; planar slip due to shearing of κ'-carbides by dislocations; TWIP suppressed at high Al.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The intergranular κ*-phase is much coarser and can result in a severe loss in ductility; intergranular κ*-carbides alone can result in a severe loss in impact energy at both room and subzero temperatures.

interfaces.interface_notes: The intergranular κ*-carbides and β-Mn precipitates are detrimental to ductility and toughness; aging temperature should be controlled below the solvus of intergranular κ*-carbide.
interfaces.phase_evolution: At higher aging temperatures / longer times κ-carbides precipitate not only coherently within the austenite matrix but also on grain boundaries as coarser particles; cellular transformation γ→γ+κ+α and β-Mn precipitation can occur at grain boundaries (b0132, b0134, b0145).

phase_interfaces.coherence: grain boundary κ* generally has a parallel orientation relationship with one of the neighbouring grains

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The ingots are homogenised at 1100–1250 °C for 1 to 3 h. For austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels, hot working (reheating and hot rolling) is conducted in the single γ phase region, and after reheating at 1100–1250 °C for a sufficient length of time the elemental segregation in the as-cast material can be largely homogenised.

Hot rolled to 2–5 mm thickness at a finishing temperature of about 850–1000 °C. In austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels recrystallization occurs during conventional hot rolling giving an equiaxed austenitic grain structure containing annealing twins. Slabs may be reheated a few times between passes to avoid cracking.

processing_steps.method: simulated coiling or direct cooling after hot rolling
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: After hot rolling the hot rolled strips are cooled to a temperature between 500 and 650 °C for 1–5 h to simulate the coiling procedure for conventional HSLA steels, or directly water-cooled, or air-cooled to room temperature. The cooling rate after hot rolling should be high enough to avoid the formation of intergranular κ-carbides.

For cold rolled products, the austenitic strips are cold rolled (e.g. 50–70% thickness reduction reported for specific alloys) prior to solution treatment. Cold rolling prior to aging retards the subsequent aging process.
For age-hardenable austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels the cold rolled strips are solution treated in the temperature range 900–1100 °C in the single austenite phase area.

processing_steps.cooling_medium: water, oil or other quench media
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: After solution treatment the strips are quenched in water, oil or other quench media to room temperature. The austenitic steels are usually fast cooled (water quenched) from solution treatment temperatures (~900–1100 °C) to room temperature to avoid the formation of coarse κ-carbide and/or α-particles.

The common practice for age hardening is to hold isothermally for 5–20 h in the temperature range 500–700 °C; the common practice is 550 °C for ~16–24 h, and Fig. 31 data include aging at 550 °C for 16 h and 24 h. Aging produces precipitation hardening through homogeneous intragranular κ'-carbide precipitation. Aging below 500 °C greatly extends the time for grain-boundary κ* formation.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Aging of austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels: first range 450–650 °C (fine coherent κ' within austenite), second range 650–800 °C (κ' both within matrix and on grain boundaries)

yield_strength.value: 100–350 MPa precipitation strengthening by κ'-phase (volume fraction ≈ 0.05–0.35)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Brinell hardness ageing curves of austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys (aged at 450–600 °C for Fe-30Mn-8Al-1C-0.35Si, and 550 °C for a series of alloys)

hardness.region: bulk, Fe-29Mn-4.9Al-0.98C and Fe-34Mn-7.1Al-0.5C aged at 550 °C (no age hardening)

hardness.value: peak hardness increases for longer times at lower aging temperatures (450 °C still rising at 1000 h)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Aged 24 h after solution treatment (1100 °C/2 h, water quenched); fully austenitic Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl series [6,9,82]

ultimate_tensile_strength.value: strong age-hardening effect only when Al content higher than 8% (aged UTS rises steeply above ~8 wt% Al); aging greatly reduces both UTS and TE of the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C steel but only weakly affects alloys with 2–7% Al

ultimate_tensile_strength.value: peak strength increment ≈ 350 MPa when C is increased from 1.3% to 1.8%

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: TEM/SEM characterization of aged austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels (Fe-30.5Mn-2.1Al-1.2C, Fe-30.4Mn-8Al-1.2C, Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.8C)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Aging conditions (< 100 h at 600 °C) and lattice parameter comparison in the γ (FCC) matrix

phases_present.crystal_structure: ordered L'12 / perovskite E21 (L'12 ordered FCC)
phases_present.morphology: initially cube-shaped, coarsens/transforms toward plate-like morphology with prolonged aging

precipitates.coherency: coherent with matrix, cube-on-cube orientation relationship [100]κ//[100]γ and [010]κ//[010]γ, lattice misfit < 3%
precipitates.distribution: homogeneous within the austenite matrix; matrix channels of width ~2–3 nm at high volume fraction

phases_present.morphology: initially discrete particles, becomes nearly continuous thin film along grain boundaries; after long aging grows into adjacent grains forming lamellar structure

precipitates.coherency: grain boundary κ* generally has a parallel orientation relationship with one of the neighbouring grains
precipitates.distribution: heterogeneous precipitation along γ/γ grain boundaries

size.value: about 3–6 times larger than those obtained after solutionizing, quenching and aging at ~550 °C

structures.overall_structure: Solution treated, quenched and aged austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steel: a single-phase austenitic (γ, FCC) matrix containing homogeneously distributed nano-sized intragranular κ'-carbide (L'12) precipitates and, after longer aging times / higher aging temperatures, coarser intergranular κ*-carbide at γ/γ grain boundaries; α-ferrite (which may order to B2/DO3) can also form.

unmapped_findings: Age hardening is not a necessary step for automotive applications of austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels but can be a consequence of the overaging regime found in many continuous annealing lines (b0299).
Aging temperature should be controlled below the solvus of intergranular κ*-carbide and aging time limited to avoid formation of the detrimental intergranular κ* phase and β-Mn precipitates (b0149).

For Fe–Mn–Al–C steels with high Al and high C, aged specimens show a nearly horizontal stress–strain curve with little or no strain hardening, and even negative work hardening rate is observed in highly alloyed steels; the underlying microstructural reason is still subject to further analysis (b0202, b0321).

Cold rolling prior to aging retards the subsequent aging process, and with sufficient aging time after cold rolling higher mechanical property values are attained; however the γ→α+β-Mn reaction is accelerated making the alloy extremely brittle, whereas warm rolling before aging appears to suppress this reaction (b0256).
